metadata.case_name: HONG YAU KAI v. CHAN CHOI SHUN AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: daily paid motor vehicle mechanic (employed by Gammon Ltd)

source: As a result of the accident the Plaintiff was injured and suffered a laceration to the scalp and a bruised left knee.
injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of head

source: As a result of the accident the Plaintiff was injured and suffered a laceration to the scalp and a bruised left knee.

injuries.description: anosmia (total loss of smell) due to injury to the olfactory nerve
source: Dr. Wu diagnosed anosmia or total loss of smell which he found to be due to an injury to the olfactory nerve .He further diagnosed vascular hypertension and cervical spondylosis.
I find the Plaintiff's condition of anosmia too I find on balance to have resulted from the trauma sustained in the accident.

injuries.description: cervical spondylosis (pre-existing, aggravated by the accident) with signs of pressure on the cervical spinal cord and resultant spasticity
source: Dr. Wu diagnosed anosmia or total loss of smell which he found to be due to an injury to the olfactory nerve .He further diagnosed vascular hypertension and cervical spondylosis.
Fifteen months later in February of 1986 Dr. Wu again examined the Plaintiff. His examination revealed stiffness of the neck with a limitation of lateral movement.

He found post-traumatic anosmia to be still present and noticed a deterioration in the condition of cervical spondylosis. He also discovered signs which indicated pressure on the cervical spinal cord and further noted some spasticity in the Plaintiff's arm which resulted in his being less dexterous.
It was his view that unless Homg's cervical spondylosis were properly cured it would be very unlikely that he could ever again work as a motor mechanic.
injuries.icd_description: Other incomplete cord syndrome of cervical spinal cord

source: Dr. Wu diagnosed anosmia or total loss of smell which he found to be due to an injury to the olfactory nerve .He further diagnosed vascular hypertension and cervical spondylosis.

manifestations.description: headache and dizzyness whenever he bent his head or worked under a vehicle (described as a sensation of a swelling or ballooning effect in his head)
diminished sense of taste (unable to detect sour taste of duck soup)
loss of memory (forgetfulness, e.g. forgot to replace brake linings)
stiffness of the neck with a limitation of lateral movement
spasticity in the Plaintiff's arm resulting in being less dexterous
pain/tenderness associated with bruised left knee

treatments_received: taken by ambulance to Princess Margaret hospital and detained
medical examinations by Dr. MA, Dr. Wedderburn, Dr. Peter Wu and Dr. Fung

losses.description: Total loss of smell (anosmia) with diminished enjoyment of food and reduced sense of taste
Permanent loss of earnings and diminished earning capacity; inability to perform the quality or amount of work as a motor mechanic
Loss of memory and forgetfulness affecting competence to work
